checks: Re-read q32_resolved.py/q32_tk.py/logs: numbers in report match out/q32 (S s=0.51 point fit / 0.47 MC median, T0=33, ff(0.26)=0.79 point / 0.77 MC; N s=0.29/0.27, ff 0.55/0.52). Agree the cores are resolved at 0.18" (T_b falls 35->30->25->19 K from native to 0.57"; radial HWHM 0.27"/0.21" vs 0.09" beam): this is robust and model-independent.

Independent refit (team/checks/q32_check.py) of the same 7 matched-beam T_b with a core + extended Gaussian whose size is FREE (instead of the constant pedestal): S s=0.37", ff(0.26")=0.67; N s=0.20", ff(0.26")=0.38. Pedestal-free single Gaussian gives ff(0.26")=0.89 (S) and 0.97 (N). So ff(0.26") spans 0.67-0.89 (S) and 0.38-0.97 (N) depending on the profile assumption; the quoted 0.73-0.80 / 0.42-0.60 are statistical errors within ONE model (constant additive pedestal). The 'medium' confidence and the +-0.1" model error on s understate this.

Logic of the Tk bound: ff<1 RAISES Tk, so Tk(ff=1) remains the only rigorous lower limit; a measured ff of a smooth Gaussian does not exclude sub-0.18" clumping (the worker admits this in the uncertainty field). 'Replaces ff=1 bound' / 'ff=0.5 not supported at S' is therefore an over-claim: it holds only if the gas is smooth inside the core (Brunetti+2021 argue smooth to 55 pc, which could be cited as the supporting assumption, but it is an assumption).

The S>=44 K headline divides T_b(0.26") = Te+T0*ff (core+pedestal, 37 K RJ-equivalent) by the core-only ff: this assigns the pedestal's emission to the core and double counts. The consistent core-only number is the deconvolved T0 (38.4-38.9 K at S; 18-19 K at N), which the worker also lists, but the text leads with 44/29-30 K. Disagree with leading with these.

Requested comparison of 0.26" vs 1.0" flux at matched uv: not given explicitly. From the table, Tb*theta^2 (flux in the beam) rises x5.7 (S) and x8.6 (N) from 0.26" to 1.0", i.e. the 0.26" beam recovers 0.18 (S)/0.12 (N) of the 1" peak flux; state this directly as the model-independent result.

Measurement is one peak channel (2.5 km/s) at a fixed pixel; HCN-window mean (used by the other Tk/density results) is 0.64x lower at S and its size was not fitted, so ff for the quantity actually used elsewhere is untested.

fixes.what: Restate Q32b: the rigorous lower limits stay ff=1 values with the deconvolved core (S>=38 K, N>=18-19 K for R=40-90; observed-0.26" S>=36 K) and give the ff-corrected values (S ~38/0.67-0.89 -> up to ~50 K; N up to ~45 K for ff 0.4) only as 'if smooth inside the core'. Remove the core+pedestal/ff(core) number (44 K, 29-30 K) or label it as inconsistent. Drop 'replaces' and the 'ff=0.5/0.3 not supported' sentence or condition it on smoothness.
fixes.why: Tk lower bounds must not be raised by a ff that only measures a smooth envelope; double counting the pedestal inflates the bound.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Standard practice: Tk bound with ff=1 is a limit; ff<1 enters as a stated assumption, with sub-beam clumping listed as the open systematic.

fixes.what: Propagate profile-model dependence into ff: report ff(0.26") and s for at least (i) constant pedestal, (ii) core+extended Gaussian with free size, (iii) single Gaussian (and, if possible, exponential/Moffat core), with the resulting Tk range; set confidence 'low' for ff and quote the S 0.67-0.89, N 0.38-0.97 envelope (or the one the extended fits give).
fixes.why: One 3-parameter model fit to 7 strongly correlated points (same cube, same pixel) cannot define ff; chi2=0.4 shows errors are loose, not that the model is right.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Experts fit the beam-convolved model directly (image plane, local background plane, or visibilities) and compare several radial profile families.

fixes.what: Do a direct image-plane/uv fit: fit (Gaussian core + free-size extended or local plane) convolved with the 0.18" CLEAN beam to the native peak-channel map within ~+-1" with the neighbouring clump masked or modelled (worker's q32_map_fit failed by locking on a clump; add the clump as a second component). Alternatively restore the 2015.1.00714.S visibilities and run uvmodelfit/uv-amplitude vs uv-distance on a line channel, which gives the size with no deconvolution or missing-flux ambiguity.
fixes.why: Convolving the clean image and fitting T_b(theta) at one pixel is sensitive to neighbouring clumps (the 1.7" point) and the pedestal degeneracy with missing flux.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Compact-source sizes are measured in the uv plane (uv-amplitude profile) or by forward-modelled 2D fits.

fixes.what: Repeat the T_b(theta) fit for the HCN-window-mean (or at least 3-channel mean) T_b, and state ff for that measure; give the explicit 0.26"/1.0" flux ratio as the first sentence of Q32a.
fixes.why: The HCN/density analyses use window means, not the peak channel; the user's Q32 asked for the flux comparison.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Match the velocity measure to the one the Tk/density result is applied to.
